pack.name: EU NIS2 directive-level baseline
pack.jurisdiction: European Union with Member State transposition
pack.source_version: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 applicability marker
coverage: all ten Article 21(2) minimum measure families, proportionality, supply-chain review and correction
Article 23 significant-incident test and complete staged reporting sequence
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 applicability and assessment marker
known_gaps: Entity scope and enforcement depend on the applicable Member State transposition and authority decisions.
Sector-specific Union-law equivalence under Article 4 needs a dedicated legal analysis.
The detailed Annex controls and sector thresholds in Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 are signalled but not decomposed into every sub-requirement in this directive-level pack.
National notification channels, forms and additional timelines require jurisdiction profiles.
pack.notice: This pack provides the EU directive-level baseline. It does not replace the applicable national law or competent-authority guidance.

fact_catalog.question: Is the organisation classified as an essential entity, important entity, outside scope or unresolved under the applicable national transposition?
Which Annex I, Annex II, special-entity or Member State identification bases support scope?
Has the applicable Member State transposition and competent authority been identified?
Does sector-specific Union law displace Articles 21 and 23 under the Article 4 equivalence test?
Does the management body approve and oversee Article 21 measures?
Do management-body members complete the required cybersecurity training?
Is regular cybersecurity training offered to employees?
Are measures selected using exposure, size, likelihood, severity, societal and economic impact?
Are risk-analysis and information-system-security policies implemented?
Is incident handling implemented?
Are business continuity, backup, disaster recovery and crisis management implemented?
Is supply-chain security implemented for direct suppliers and service providers?
Is security integrated into acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure?
Are policies and procedures used to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity measures?
Are basic cyber-hygiene practices and cybersecurity training implemented?
Are policies and procedures for cryptography and appropriate encryption implemented?
Are human-resources security, access control and asset management implemented?
Are appropriate multi-factor or continuous authentication and secure communications implemented?
Does supply-chain review address supplier vulnerabilities, product quality and secure development?
Can identified non-compliance be corrected without undue delay?
Does an incident meet the Article 23 significant-impact test?
Is the significant incident still ongoing when the final report would be due?
Can an early warning be submitted within 24 hours of awareness?
Can an incident notification with initial assessment be submitted within 72 hours?
Can intermediate status reports be supplied when requested?
Can a final report be submitted within one month of the incident notification?
Can an ongoing-incident progress report and later final report be supplied on the required schedule?
Can service recipients be notified without undue delay when a significant incident is likely to adversely affect service?
Can potentially affected recipients receive measures or remedies for a significant cyber threat?
Is the entity one of the digital, infrastructure, managed-service or trust-service providers covered by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690?
Has the entity assessed and documented the detailed technical requirements and incident-significance criteria in Regulation (EU) 2024/2690?

anchors.locator: Articles 2 to 4 and Annexes I and II
anchors.summary: Scope, essential and important entity classification, and sector-specific Union-law equivalence.
Management-body approval, oversight, liability context and training.
Risk-proportionate all-hazards measures and the ten minimum measure families.
Significant-incident test, recipient communications and staged reporting.
Detailed technical and methodological requirements and incident-significance criteria for listed digital and trust-service entities.
